title: Asmahan Bkerat's debut documentary 'Concrete Land' moves from London Film Festival's Documentary Competition to the LPFF on 26 November.
text: 'Concrete Land' (Jordan, Palestine), Asmahan Bkerat's feature debut, follows the Al-Najjar family as an eviction notice, new construction and hostile neighbours push them and their animals off their land in Jordan. It competed in the BFI London Film Festival's Documentary Competition with screenings on 8 and 10 October, and screens at the London Palestine Film Festival at Bertha DocHouse on 26 November. Runtime is given as 100 minutes in the LFF review and 101 minutes in the LPFF listing.
tags: Asmahan Bkerat Rana Eid Concrete Land Jordan London, Bertha DocHouse

title: Three programmes of short films from Gaza screen at the London Palestine Film Festival on 16, 17 and 21 November.
text: LPFF 2026 shows five 'From Ground Zero+' shorts, including 'Gaza to Oscar' and 'Very Small Dreams', at the Barbican on 16 November (three are UK premieres, per the Barbican). A 'Gaza Shorts' programme with 'What the Sand Remembers' and 'The Scene' plays Curzon Hoxton on 17 November, and 'The Clown of Gaza' with 'One More Show' screens at Riverside Studios on 21 November.
tags: From Ground Zero+ (shorts programme) Gaza Shorts The Clown of Gaza / One More Show Barbican Centre Curzon Hoxton Riverside Studios

title: Nicolas Wadimoff's Gaza documentary 'Who Is Still Alive', Switzerland's Oscar entry, opens the London Palestine Film Festival at the Barbican on 13 November.
text: 'Who Is Still Alive' ('Qui vit encore') is built from the testimonies of nine Palestinians who fled Gaza and redraw their neighbourhoods in chalk; it was filmed in South Africa and contains no bombardment or archive footage. It premiered in the Giornate degli Autori at Venice in 2025, won the Prix de Soleure at Solothurn, and is Switzerland's submission for Best International Feature at the 99th Oscars. Its UK premiere opens the London Palestine Film Festival at the Barbican on 13 November, followed by a talk with Wadimoff and producer Jawdat Khoudary, with a second screening on 14 November.
tags: Nicolas Wadimoff Jawdat Khoudary Who Is Still Alive Gaza South Africa Barbican Centre, London

title: Watermelon Pictures opens 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' in US cinemas on 30 October, starting at the Quad in New York.
text: Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans's 84-minute documentary re-investigates the October 1985 tripwire bombing in Santa Ana, California, that killed Palestinian-American teacher and activist Alex Odeh, a case never solved. It won Sundance's Special Jury Award for Journalistic Excellence and screened at the Berlinale. Watermelon Pictures, which took North American rights in June, opens it on 30 October at the Quad Cinema (New York), Laemmle Glendale and Uprising Theater (Chicago), then the Frida Cinema in Santa Ana (5-10 Nov), Hudson NY (6 Nov) and New Orleans (13 Nov). It also plays Boston (18 Oct), Athens (24 Oct), El Gouna and the LPFF UK premiere (14 Nov).
tags: Jason Osder William Lafi Youmans Alex Odeh Who Killed Alex Odeh? Santa Ana, California Quad Cinema, New York Laemmle Glendale Uprising Theater, Chicago Frida Cinema, Santa Ana New Orleans

title: Ten months after his death, Mohammad Bakri gets tributes in Athens (25 Oct) and London (19-20 Nov, with Saleh Bakri).
text: Actor-director Mohammad Bakri, best known for 'Jenin, Jenin', died on 24 December 2025 aged 72 after heart and lung problems, AP reported. The Athens Palestine Film Festival holds a special event, 'Mohammad Bakri: A Cultural Legacy', at the Trianon on 25 October 2026. The London Palestine Film Festival screens 'A Life in Cinema: A Tribute to Mohammad Bakri' (124 min) at the Rio Cinema on 19 November and Riverside Studios on 20 November, each followed by a discussion with his son, actor Saleh Bakri.
tags: Mohammad Bakri Saleh Bakri Adam Bakri A Life in Cinema: A Tribute to Mohammad Bakri Jenin, Jenin Athens, Trianon Cinema London, Rio Cinema London, Riverside Studios

title: Nai Barghouti performs 'Music of Palestine' at HKUST's Shaw Auditorium in Hong Kong on 25 October.
text: Singer and flautist Nai Barghouti plays the last listed concert of HKUST's Cosmopolis Festival, 'Music of Palestine' on 25 October 2026 at 19:30. Her ensemble mixes original songs with arrangements of classic Arabic repertoire, jazz and Western classical music. She also featured on MC Abdul's 2026 single 'Wait for Me'.
tags: Nai Barghouti Shaw Auditorium, HKUST, Hong Kong

title: Faraj Suleiman plays his first fully solo show, 'Faraj, Piano and Mic', in Edmonton on 24 October; a Ziad Rahbani tribute at the Barbican follows on 23 January 2027.
text: Palestinian pianist and composer Faraj Suleiman performs 'Faraj, Piano and Mic' at the Horowitz Theatre in Edmonton on 24 October 2026, billed as his first completely solo show: one piano, one microphone, no band, in Arabic, with songs from 'Better than Berlin', 'Second Verse' and 'Maryam'. MARSM has also announced Suleiman leading a 20-piece ensemble and guest singers in a tribute to Ziad Rahbani at London's Barbican on 23 January 2027.

title: Alex Bakri's 'Habibi Hussein', about Cinema Jenin's last projectionist, screens in Athens (23 Oct), Boston (24 Oct) and at the Barbican (18 Nov).
text: 'Habibi Hussein' is Alex Bakri's debut feature, built from footage he shot in 2008-2010 while working as cinematographer on the NGO-backed reopening of Cinema Jenin. It turns the focus to projectionist Hussein Darbi, who began working at the cinema at 12 alongside his uncle, and questions the foreign project that later sidelined him; the cinema was demolished seven years after reopening, per The New Arab. It screens at the Athens Palestine Film Festival on 23 October, at Coolidge Corner Theatre for Boston PFF on 24 October and at the Barbican for LPFF on 18 November with a ScreenTalk.
tags: Alex Bakri Hussein Darbi Markus Vetter Habibi Hussein Cinema Jenin, Jenin Athens Coolidge Corner Theatre Barbican Centre

title: Abdallah Al-Khatib's Berlinale prize-winner 'Chronicles from the Siege' plays London's Dare strand and Boston's MFA on 23 October.
text: 'Chronicles from the Siege' by Palestinian-Syrian director Abdallah Al-Khatib draws on his years in the Yarmouk refugee camp and won the GWFF Best First Feature Award at the 76th Berlinale. It closed the Toronto Palestine Film Festival on 4 October, is in the Dare strand of the BFI London Film Festival, and screens at the MFA Boston on 23 October, co-presented with the Institute for Palestine Studies.

title: The 15th DC Palestinian Film and Arts Festival screens 22-25 October at the Angelika Pop-Up at Union Market.
text: The DC Palestinian Film and Arts Festival, founded in 2011 and run by volunteers, marks its 15th year from 22 to 25 October 2026. Its 2026 film programme of shorts, dramas and documentaries is set for the Angelika Pop-Up at Union Market in Washington. The festival's site was still a 'save the date' notice with titles to come.
tags: Angelika Pop-Up at Union Market, Washington, D.C.

title: BFI London Film Festival (7-18 Oct) has 'Concrete Land' in its Documentary Competition; winners are announced 18 October.
text: The 70th BFI London Film Festival runs 7-18 October 2026. Asmahan Bkerat's 'Concrete Land' (Jordan, Palestine), a 100-minute documentary about the displaced Al-Najjar family in Jordan, is in the Documentary Competition and screened on 8 and 10 October. Abdallah Al-Khatib's 'Chronicles from the Siege' plays in the Dare strand, Amer Nasser's short 'To the North' in the Altered States shorts programme, and Mohanad Yaqubi's 'Revolutionaries Never Die' screened at the ICA on 12 October. The BFI says award winners are revealed on Sunday 18 October.

title: Gaza-born rapper MC Abdul releases his debut album 'Day by Day, Shway Shway' on EMPIRE on 16 October.
text: MC Abdul, 18 and now based in the Bay Area, releases his nine-track debut album 'Day by Day, Shway Shway' on 16 October 2026 through EMPIRE, with Suhel Nafar, head of EMPIRE's West Asia and North Africa division, as executive producer. Singles before the album included 'Wait for Me' (with Nai Barghouti), 'Wein Abdul?' and 'Shway Shway', produced by !llmind. He performs at Palestine Culture Day in Redwood City on 17 October.
tags: MC Abdul Suhel Nafar !llmind Nai Barghouti Day by Day, Shway Shway Shway Shway San Francisco Bay Area Redwood City

title: The 20th Boston Palestine Film Festival runs 16-25 October, opening at the MFA with 'Edward Said: Between Worlds' and closing with 'Palestine Comedy Club'.
text: The 20th Boston Palestine Film Festival opens on 16 October 2026 at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston with Maiken Baird's 'Edward Said: Between Worlds' (listed as sold out) and closes on 25 October at the Coolidge Corner Theatre with 'Palestine Comedy Club'. Screenings include 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' (18 Oct, MFA), Kamal Aljafari's 'With Hasan in Gaza' (19 Oct, Coolidge), 'Traces of Home' (20 Oct, Brattle Theatre), 'Chronicles from the Siege' (23 Oct, MFA), and 'Habibi Hussein' and 'Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep' (24 Oct, Coolidge). Other venues are BU's Howard Thurman Center, MassArt and UMass Amherst.

title: Maiken Baird's 'Edward Said: Between Worlds' opens the Boston Palestine Film Festival on 16 October after its TIFF Docs world premiere.
text: The 107-minute documentary profiles Edward Said largely in his own words, drawing on decades of archive footage and interviews, and covers 'Orientalism', 'The Question of Palestine', 1948 and the Oslo Accords. It world-premiered in TIFF Docs on 12 September 2026. It opens the Boston Palestine Film Festival at the MFA on 16 October (sold out, Q&A with producer Sarah Mowaswes) and screens at the London Palestine Film Festival on 15 November (Cine Lumiere, with Baird) and 22 November (Rio Cinema).
tags: Maiken Baird Edward Said Sarah Mowaswes Edward Said: Between Worlds Toronto Museum of Fine Arts Boston London, Cine Lumiere London, Rio Cinema

title: The ninth El Gouna Film Festival opens in Egypt on 15 October and runs to 23 October; 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' is among its first ten announced titles.
text: El Gouna Film Festival's ninth edition opens on 15 October 2026 with the French film 'All About Corinne' by Marc Fitoussi and runs until 23 October. In August the festival named ten titles for the edition, the tenth being 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' by Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, an investigative documentary about the 1985 killing of Palestinian-American activist Alex Odeh. Asharq (22 Sep) puts the line-up at 36 features plus 17 shorts; that report names no Palestinian titles beyond the Odeh film.
tags: Jason Osder William Lafi Youmans Marc Fitoussi Andrew Mohsen Who Killed Alex Odeh? El Gouna, Egypt

title: Athens Palestine Film Festival 2026 opens on 15 October at the Trianon Cinema with Elia Suleiman's 'It Must Be Heaven' and runs to 31 October.
text: The Athens Palestine Film Festival (APFF26) runs 15-31 October 2026 at the Trianon Cinema, the National Museum of Contemporary Art (EMST) and Onassis Stegi. It opens on 15 October at 20:00 with Elia Suleiman's 'It Must Be Heaven'. The programme also includes 'Habibi Hussein' (23 Oct), 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' (24 Oct), Larissa Sansour's 'A Sunken Tale of Losses Delayed' (29-30 Oct) and a special event, 'Mohammad Bakri: A Cultural Legacy' (25 Oct).

title: The 30th Jerusalem Festival, run by the Yabous Cultural Centre, reaches the scheduled end of its two-month run on 15 October.
text: The Jerusalem Festival returned on 16 August 2026 at the Yabous Cultural Centre in East Jerusalem after a pause since summer 2023, opening with a tribute to Ziad Rahbani played by the Jerusalem Arabic Music Ensemble. AFP reported it would run two months, until 15 October, with concerts, talks and exhibitions at venues across East Jerusalem. Sharjah24 calls it the 30th edition. Yabous board chairman Suheil Khoury said the festival returns to give people hope.
tags: Suheil Khoury Yousef al-Salhi Ziad Rahbani Yabous Cultural Centre, East Jerusalem

title: All four Elia Suleiman features screen in Athens between 15 and 31 October as part of the Athens Palestine Film Festival.
text: The Athens Palestine Film Festival programmes Elia Suleiman's four features: 'It Must Be Heaven' opens the festival on 15 October, 'The Time That Remains' plays on 16 October and 'Divine Intervention' on 18 October, all at the Trianon, and 'Chronicle of a Disappearance' closes the run at Onassis Stegi on 31 October.

title: Rakan Mayasi's 'Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep' competes in Progressive Cinema at the Rome Film Festival (13-25 Oct), then plays Seminci in Valladolid 29-31 Oct.
text: Rakan Mayasi's debut feature 'Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep', a Belgium-Lebanon-Palestine-Qatar-Saudi co-production that premiered in Cannes' Un Certain Regard on 20 May 2026, is one of 18 films in the Rome Film Festival's Progressive Cinema competition and is also listed for its best documentary and best first feature awards. Rome's 21st edition runs 13-25 October. Seminci (Valladolid, 23-31 October) screens it in its Meeting Point section on 29, 30 and 31 October. Boston Palestine Film Festival shows it on 24 October.

title: Cairo International Film Festival unveiled a 145-film line-up for its 47th edition, 11-20 November; its president said 'We will never forget Palestine.'
text: The 47th Cairo International Film Festival, marking 50 years since its 1976 launch, runs 11-20 November 2026 with 145 films from 64 countries, including 17 world premieres and 87 MENA premieres. Ahram Online reports that the Palestinian cause remains part of the programme, quoting CIFF president Hussein Fahmy, but the report names no Palestinian titles. In 2025 Cairo gave three awards to 'Once Upon a Time in Gaza'.
tags: Hussein Fahmy Cairo

title: The Palestine Film Institute presented four works-in-progress, including a film about Gaza's first rock band, at its third Palestine Showcase at the Durban FilmMart.
text: TimesLIVE reported on 12 October that the Palestine Film Institute brought a filmmaker delegation and four projects to its 2026 Palestine Film Hub Showcase at the Durban FilmMart, the third such showcase. The projects are 'On the Sea Road', 'Echoes of the Unsung' (Gaza's first rock band trying to record an album), 'A Sole Survivor' (a Gaza man who is his family's only survivor) and 'Within Sight and Sound'. Filmmaker Jihan El-Tahri said 22 short films were made in Gaza on mobile phones during the war.
tags: Jihan El-Tahri On the Sea Road Echoes of the Unsung A Sole Survivor Within Sight and Sound Durban, South Africa Gaza Chicago

title: 'Citizen Osama' by Ahmed Hassouna is Palestine's entry for Best International Feature at the 99th Academy Awards; the 15-film shortlist is due 15 December.
text: Palestinian Culture Minister Imad Hamdan announced on 31 August that Ahmed Hassouna's 69-minute documentary 'Citizen Osama' would represent Palestine, on the recommendation of an independent committee; The National counts it as Palestine's 19th submission in the category since 2003. The film follows Osama Al-Ashi, a former art photographer documenting the war in northern Gaza while protecting his wife and newborn child, and premiered out of competition in Venice. The Academy's submission deadline was 30 September; the shortlist comes on 15 December 2026, nominations on 21 January 2027 and the ceremony on 14 March 2027 in Los Angeles.
tags: Ahmed Hassouna Osama Al-Ashi Imad Hamdan Citizen Osama Northern Gaza Venice Los Angeles

title: Muayad Alayan's 'Conversation With the Sea' moves from Venice and Toronto to Doha's competition (19-27 Nov) and closes the London Palestine Film Festival on 27 November.
text: Muayad Alayan's 112-minute 'Conversation With the Sea', written with Rami Alayan and starring Kamel El Basha, world-premiered in Venice Spotlight on 7 September 2026 and had its North American premiere in TIFF's Centerpiece. It is a Palestine-Netherlands-Saudi Arabia-Qatar co-production; MAD World holds worldwide sales except Benelux. It makes its MENA premiere in the Doha Film Festival competition and is the closing film of the London Palestine Film Festival at Curzon Mayfair on 27 November.

title: Berlin's AL.Festival (2-10 October, Festsaal Kreuzberg) included oud player Kamilya Jubran and rapper Daboor.
text: AL.Festival's 2026 edition ran from 2 to 10 October at Festsaal Kreuzberg in Berlin. Its announced line-up included Palestinian oud player and composer Kamilya Jubran, Palestinian rapper Daboor of BLTNM, Tunisian singer Badiaa Bouhrizi, Egyptian producer Abadir and a showcase from the Syrian Cassette Archives.
tags: Kamilya Jubran Daboor Badiaa Bouhrizi Abadir Festsaal Kreuzberg, Berlin

title: London Palestine Film Festival 2026 runs 13-27 November across a dozen London venues, from the Barbican to Curzon Mayfair.
text: The London Palestine Film Festival returns 13-27 November 2026, opening at the Barbican with 'Who Is Still Alive' and closing on 27 November at Curzon Mayfair with 'Conversation with the Sea'. The programme includes the UK premiere of 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?' (14 Nov, ICA), 'Edward Said: Between Worlds' (15 Nov, Cine Lumiere; 22 Nov, Rio), 'From Ground Zero+' shorts from Gaza (16 Nov, Barbican), 'Habibi Hussein' (18 Nov, Barbican), 'Gaza's Twins, Come Back to Me' (22 Nov) and 'Concrete Land' (26 Nov, Bertha DocHouse). Other venues include Curzon Hoxton, Curzon Soho, Riverside Studios, The Garden Cinema, Sands Films and Ropetackle in Shoreham.

title: The 19th Toronto Palestine Film Festival ended its online window on 9 October after in-person screenings from 30 September to 4 October.
text: The 19th Toronto Palestine Film Festival ran in person from 30 September to 4 October 2026, opening with 'Endless Sunlight' and Annemarie Jacir's 'Palestine 36' and closing with Abdallah Al-Khatib's 'Chronicles from the Siege'; selected films streamed on Eventive until 9 October. The programme included 'Who Killed Alex Odeh?', 'Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep', 'Edward Said: Between Worlds', 'Palestine Comedy Club', a 'Views from Gaza' shorts programme and a live show, 'TPFF presents: NARCY x Excentrik', on 3 October.
tags: Annemarie Jacir Abdallah Al-Khatib Rakan Mayasi NARCY Excentrik Palestine 36 Endless Sunlight Chronicles from the Siege Toronto

title: Doha Film Festival named its 15-film international competition on 8 October; 'Thirteen in Gaza' and 'Conversation with the Sea' make their MENA premieres there, 19-27 November.
text: The Doha Film Festival announced 15 films for its 2026 International Feature Film Competition on 8 October, 11 of them supported by Doha Film Institute grants and seven directed by women. Arab News confirms Hosam Abu Dan's 'Thirteen in Gaza' and Muayad Alayan's 'Conversation with the Sea' will make their Middle East and North Africa premieres in the competition. Trade coverage (Screen Daily, Turkiye Today) lists four Palestinian titles, adding Rabab Khamis's 'Sama' (world premiere) and Mohanad Yaqubi's 'Revolutionaries Never Die'. Prizes include USD 75,000 for best narrative and USD 50,000 for best documentary.
tags: Hosam Abu Dan Muayad Alayan Rabab Khamis Mohanad Yaqubi Thirteen in Gaza Conversation with the Sea Sama Revolutionaries Never Die Doha, Qatar

title: The National's best Arabic songs of 2026 list includes Saint Levant and Tul8te's 'Nano', a No. 1 on Spotify Egypt.
text: The National's 5 October list of the best Arabic songs of 2026 includes 'Nano' by Tul8te and Saint Levant (1 June), which it says reached No. 1 on Spotify in Egypt and stayed in the top 10 through the summer. It also picks 'Dawaween' by Jordanian rapper Shbash with Palestinian artist Rknddn (13 February) and 'Nassaba' by Jordanian-Palestinian singer Siilawy (17 April).

title: Rasha Nahas released the single 'Manaqish' on 25 September; her Meshell Ndegeocello-produced third album, billed for October, has no listed date yet.
text: Haifa-born, Berlin-based Rasha Nahas released the single 'Manaqish' on 25 September 2026. HAU Hebbel am Ufer, which hosted her preview concert on 21 May, said her next album, produced by Meshell Ndegeocello, would be released in October; Wikipedia still lists it as forthcoming and Apple Music shows no pre-release. Apple Music lists a Berlin concert at Festsaal Kreuzberg on 14 November.
tags: Rasha Nahas Meshell Ndegeocello Manaqish Berlin Festsaal Kreuzberg

title: 'Thirteen in Gaza' by Hosam Abu Dan won TIFF 2026's NETPAC Award; it had its Western New York premiere on 12 October and heads to Doha in November.
text: Hosam Abu Dan's 77-minute 'Thirteen in Gaza', described as the first fiction feature shot in Gaza in 12 years, won the NETPAC Award at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, where it premiered in Centerpiece. It is produced by New Scene for Media Production with support from the Doha Film Institute and the Arab Fund for Arts and Culture; Watermelon Pictures handles North American distribution and MAD World world sales. The Buffalo International Film Festival screened it on 12 October at the North Park Theatre.

title: Together for Palestine says its benefit concert is 'coming to New York City soon'; no date, venue or line-up has been named.
text: Together for Palestine announced plans for a New York fundraising concert on Instagram on 17 September 2026, a year after its Wembley Arena show of 17 September 2025, according to DJ Mag. The organisation's website says the event is 'coming to New York City soon' and offers ticket alerts, with no date, venue or line-up. The London concert featured Palestinian artists including Saint Levant, Elyanna, Nai Barghouti, Sama' Abdulhadi and Faraj Suleiman.
tags: Brian Eno Saint Levant Elyanna Nai Barghouti Sama' Abdulhadi Faraj Suleiman Lana Lubany New York Wembley Arena, London

title: Saint Levant moved the North American leg of his Afandi World Tour to spring 2027 over US visa checks, so this week's original Los Angeles and San Diego dates are off.
text: Saint Levant (Marwan Abdelhamid) released his second album, 'Afandi', his first entirely in Arabic, on 21 August 2026. On 2 September he postponed the North American leg of the Afandi World Tour after his US visa, initially approved, was sent for additional background checks; the leg now opens in Ottawa on 19 March 2027, with Boston on 27 March as the first US date, and tickets are honoured or refunded. The original plan had him at The Wiltern, Los Angeles on 13-14 October and in San Diego on 15 October. The National still lists a 19 December show at Dopa World in Dubai.
tags: Saint Levant Afandi Ottawa Boston Dubai

title: Mohanad Yaqubi's 'Revolutionaries Never Die', a letter to filmmaker Jocelyne Saab, won a Special Jury Prize at Locarno and is now in London and Doha.
text: Mohanad Yaqubi's 80-minute documentary (Palestine/Belgium/Qatar) reframes footage shot by Lebanese director Jocelyne Saab across Palestine, Lebanon and Iran between 1973 and 1983, prompted by an invitation she sent him before her death. It won the Special Jury Prize CINE+OCS in Locarno's Cineasti del Presente competition in August 2026. It screened at the ICA for the BFI London Film Festival on 12 October and is listed in the Doha Film Festival competition (19-27 Nov).
tags: Mohanad Yaqubi Jocelyne Saab Revolutionaries Never Die Locarno London, ICA Doha
